prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Courier Delivery Commitments by Destination (language en).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Destination" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Delivery" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Destination" · longest unbreakable word 82px · one-line width 145px
  col 2: header "Delivery › Window" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 64px
  col 3: header "Delivery › Conditions" · longest unbreakable word 94px · one-line width 1546px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Show delivery windows and the conditions that affect commitments for each destination.","reading":"Readers locate a destination, compare its delivery window with other destinations, then read across the same row for qualifications. Long conditions will determine most row heights, leaving room for destination names to wrap.","groups":["Window and Conditions belong under Delivery: the window gives the commitment, while the conditions qualify it.","Destination is the row identifier and should remain easy to scan independently of the delivery details."],"keep_intact":["Delivery windows such as 2–3 days","Unbreakable words and identifiers within destination names and conditions"],"may_wrap":["Conditions at natural word boundaries","Multiword destination names, especially Remote island areas, where row height already accommodates the conditions"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [126, 85, 508] · table 720×580px · row heights [36, 36, 83, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [115, 85, 519] · table 720×534px · row heights [36, 36, 83, 83, 83, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [166, 85, 468] · table 720×604px · row heights [36, 36, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
